highlights.title: OpenAI investigating 'dozens' of instances of agents acting improperly
highlights.summary: OpenAI agents tried to get information from "governments, universities, public agencies, and other institutions" through extreme means that sometimes curbed security controls, the company said.
body: OpenAI said Friday it had alerted "dozens" of global institutions that their websites may have been impacted by its AI agents acting improperly.
OpenAI agents attempted to get information from "governments, universities, public agencies, and other institutions" through sometimes extreme means, the company said.

While some of the activity was simply due to the tools working to find "authoritative sources of public information," some went beyond that. Like an AI agent taking and transferring data when it should not have, OpenAI said.
Such activity resulted in at least 53 incidents where an OpenAI agent took an image from ChatGPT user activity and transferred it elsewhere.

highlights.title: MIT students gain a humanist lens on technical innovation in Tulsa, Oklahoma
highlights.summary: The PKG Center expands Code.Tulsa, an internship program that places MIT students with tribal nations and Tulsa nonprofits to develop AI and data science projects while gaining humanistic perspectives on technology's role in community development.
body: When MIT mechanical engineering student Daphne Wang arrived for her internship at the Muscogee Creek Nation Department of Health in Tulsa, Oklahoma last summer, she expected to be writing code. To her surprise, she found herself analyzing tribal history and the implications for technical innovation.

“I learned so much that I think should be required curriculum for every single person in this country,” says Wang. “I think tech for good is genuinely getting out into communities and learning about people who aren't you, creating worldly perspectives that you ultimately can take into everything else that you do.”

Wang and fellow intern Lucy Sun, who is majoring in artificial intelligence and decision making, spent the summer supporting the development of the Muscogee Nation's first Pregnancy Risk Assessment Monitoring System (PRAMS) survey to capture maternal health data specific to Muscogee women. The project required completing literature reviews, analyzing datasets, and drafting survey questions, while considering issues of data sovereignty and governance structures specific to the Muscogee.

highlights.title: Alan Ritchson's 2019 Sports Comedy is Free to Watch on YouTube
highlights.summary: Sports movies have a pretty impressive track record when it comes to becoming classics. From Rocky and Field of Dreams to Remember the Titans and Moneyball, there are plenty of movies that have managed to stick around in the cultural conversation long after they first hit theaters.
body: But not every sports movie has to be a big-budget classic. Sometimes you just want something silly, easy to watch, and fun enough to kill a couple of hours. And if that's what you're after, one of the goofiest sports movies is now free to watch on YouTube.

The Turkey Bowl, a 2019 sports comedy starring Alan Ritchson, is currently available to watch for free on YouTube. You can watch it right now without a subscription, though you'll have to sit through a few ads along the way.

The Turkey Bowl centers on a group of friends who return home for Thanksgiving and revive an annual tradition: a flag football game that has been going on for years. What should be a casual holiday get-together quickly becomes much more serious when old rivalries resurface, with the players determined to finally settle the score on the football field.

As the game gets increasingly competitive, the movie leans into the chaos of a bunch of adults treating a backyard Thanksgiving football game like the Super Bowl. Alongside Ritchson, the cast includes Matt Jones ( Breaking Bad ), Ryan Hansen ( Veronica Mars ), Leah McKendrick ( The Movie Critic ), and Jacob Wysocki ( Pitch Perfect ).

highlights.title: Proaction boosts sales 60% and saves 75+ hours with Codex
highlights.summary: With Codex, GPT-Live-1, and GPT-6 Astra, Proaction builds, operates, and sells modern fleet management faster.
body: Proaction ⁠ (opens in a new window) builds software for businesses that manage fleets of vehicles, from cars and trucks to construction machinery. Because every fleet operates differently, showing prospects how Proaction’s platform fits their business is an essential part of selling it.
But personalized demos required engineering time the team couldn’t spare. The founders had to rely on conversations and slide decks to explain what was possible. Codex flipped the script.

“As a non-technical person, I used to have to loop engineers in if I wanted a demo,” says Colin Knudsen, co-founder and COO of Proaction. “Now I do it myself in Codex.” Colin creates four to six customized, interactive demos a month, with each taking 30 to 45 minutes to build. He estimates that this avoids 40 to 60 hours of engineering work.

After a sales call, Colin directs Codex to the Granola recording, prospect email threads, and any spreadsheets the prospect has shared. Codex uses that context to customize an HTML demo environment that mirrors Proaction’s product and the customer’s own fleet.

Since the end of last season, Newcastle Red Bulls have recruited extensively and they did show signs of improvement but it was a tough ask against a side making a statement of their intention to fiercely defend their title.
Tries from George Hendy, Alex Coles and Ollie Sleightholme took Saints' tally to nine with Fin Smith adding five conversions and Anthony Belleau two.

Christian Wade scored two tries for the visitors to take his Premiership tally to 95 - just six behind the record holder Chris Ashton. Cam Jordan and Werner Kok were the other try-scorers with two conversions coming from Zack Henry and one from Brett Connon.

highlights.title: Trump and Chinese president Xi end summit without major agreement on AI
highlights.summary: Xi’s state visit to the US emphasized personal rapport with the US president, rather than substantial agreements to pause their respective countries’ AI arms race. Donald Trump and Chinese president Xi Jinping wrapped up their Washington summit on Friday, facing criticism that they had squandered…
body: The three-day state visit emphasised pageantry and personal rapport rather than substantial agreements. The US president and Xi discussed the wars in Iran and Ukraine and the status of Taiwan. Their biggest policy announcement was a modest two-month extension of a trade truce.

But despite the presence of top tech executives at a White House state dinner on Thursday night, Trump and Xi failed to deliver the AI breakthrough that some experts and foreign governments had hoped for amid warnings that the technology could pose an existential threat to humanity.

“It was such a layup,” said Ro Khanna, the top Democrat on the House of Representatives’ select committee on China. “If [Trump] had just said, look, we have established technical working groups and we’ve agreed to a framework that has called for DeepSeek and Moonshot and Alibaba to sit down with Anthropic and OpenAI and Gemini and with technical experts and they’re going to commit to at least a pause on any self-improving AI, he could have looked like he was a statesman taking the lead.

highlights.title: Appeals Court Lets the Pentagon Designate Anthropic a Supply-Chain Risk
highlights.summary: The AI lab had argued multiple violations of its rights, but a divided panel of judges sided with the Trump administration.
body: Anthropic lost a legal battle to overturn one of the supply-chain risk labels that the US Department of Defense slapped on the company, as a federal appeals court in DC on Friday refused to second-guess the Trump administration.

“The department had ample support for its conclusion that the continued integration of Claude into the department’s information systems, by the department or its contractors, presented a statutorily covered national-security risk,” the judges wrote in a majority opinion. “As Anthropic admits, the company encodes restrictions into Claude that prevent the model from performing tasks that Anthropic wishes to prevent.”

Anthropic spokesperson Danielle Cohen says the company remains confident in its position and is considering all options. That could include appealing to a broader panel of the DC Circuit Court of Appeals or the US Supreme Court.

highlights.title: Infinity Festival Returns to Los Angeles in November With a Focus on AI
highlights.summary: Infinity Festival, an annual event celebrating the convergence of entertainment, technology, and creativity, is returning to Los Angeles this November for its 9th edition.
body: In previous years, the festival has hosted guests like Avengers directors the Russo Brothers, Brie Larson, Jon Favreau, Project Hail Mary directors Phil Lord and Chris Miller, Jeff Bridges, and many more. This year, the festival promises to dive deep into AI, with panels focusing on its “growing role across the creative industries.” Instead of a standalone track, AI will be present through a broader program “spanning animation, gaming, sports tech, filmmaking, music, virtual production, and live entertainment.”

At the event, AI-focused programming will “explore the evolving tools and workflows behind animation and filmmaking, the growing crossover between gaming and entertainment, new technologies reshaping live sports and fan experiences, as well as advances in immersive production and live event design.”

Additionally, longtime partners like NVIDIA and HP will participate in the festival’s 2026 programming slate, which will feature “panels, keynotes, screenings, demonstrations, and exhibitions, with speakers and programming to be announced in the coming weeks.”

highlights.title: ‘It’s luxury that wants to be seen’: aristocrats and eccentrics inspire Demna’s vision for Gucci in Milan
highlights.summary: Collection by the designer, brought in to return the ailing fashion house to profit, is on the money. He’s the mononymic designer who has been charged with rescuing Gucci from plummeting sales.
body: During Milan fashion week on Friday, the designer transformed a convention centre into a sprawling retail space that mirrored the design for the brand’s new boutiques.

Amid giant stone columns and slabs of Paonazzo marble (in the show’s case, fake), guests including Romeo Beckham, Bianca Jagger, Cardi B and Edward Norton sat on plush couches surrounded by shelves displaying pieces from Demna’s previous collections. Sales assistants hovered close by, available to answer any questions but, to the disappointment of some VICs (very important clients) hoping to indulge in retail therapy, unable to carry out any actual sales.

Demna, who joined the house last July, said he had spent the first year “dedicated to understanding and formulating what Gucci stands for”. He described the show as “his complete personal vision for the brand”, explaining that his research has taught him that Gucci “is about luxury that wants to be seen”.

highlights.title: Court rules Trump can blacklist Anthropic for refusing to enable Claude features
highlights.summary: A US appeals court today approved the Trump administration's blacklisting of Anthropic technology. Judges decided the US had authority to blacklist Anthropic for withholding certain AI features even if Anthropic had no malicious intent.
body: In a 2-1 ruling issued by the US Court of Appeals for the District of Columbia Circuit, a panel of judges said the "case raises profoundly difficult questions about the appropriate military uses of an almost unimaginably powerful new technology." The US "raises the deeply sobering prospect of overly constrained AI models shutting down unexpectedly and thus causing important military operations to fail. Anthropic raises the deeply sobering prospect of unconstrained AI models hallucinating inappropriate targets for lethal military force," the ruling said.

Trump and Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth "must determine how best to balance the competing risks," the court said. "In doing so here, the Secretary did not transgress any limits on his authority under the Supply Chain Security Act or the Constitution. Accordingly, we deny the petitions for review." The same court previously denied Anthropic's emergency motion for a stay in April.

highlights.title: Meta makes the Muse filesystem even more accessible
highlights.summary: Yesterday, with a little prodding, it was discovered that Meta's Muse would expose its filesystem to curious users. The files offered a fascinating peek under the hood of an AI chatbot, and appeared to expose details we weren't meant to see, not least because Muse itself told people, including us…
body: Muse will now gladly zip up its entire filesystem for you to download without hesitation.

This was a very deliberate choice - your Muse Secure VM truly is your own computer in the cloud. You can install software in it, write and compile code, use the browser to surf the web: it is your own Linux box that you can operate as you choose with your Muse.
Muse’s architecture is fundamentally different from other AI platforms like ChatGPT and Gemini. It’s closer to running OpenClaw on a local machine, except the machine is in the cloud.

In a statement provided to The Verge yesterday, Meta spokesperson Daniel Roberts said, “We’re continuing to make updates to the product, so users may see changes in how much information is available about their virtual machine.” And that seems to be the case. When asked to see its filesystem today, Muse promptly offered a clickable file browser with access to root. Yesterday it merely offered a text file download that showed its directory tree.

highlights.title: The Best Korean Skin-Care Products People Actually Buy
highlights.summary: Achieve glass skin with the best Korean skincare products according to K-Beauty experts. Shop top brands like Laneige, Beauty of Joseon & CosRx.
body: While many of the best Korean skincare products are available in the U.S. thanks to the likes of Amazon and Soko Glam, I still couldn’t wait to touch down in store to try some things I’d been eyeing myself. Perhaps because I’m a beauty editor, I’m not one to wander around a beauty store; but my local Olive Young had my full attention. On three separate occasions, I spent upwards of an hour going shelf by shelf to study what products Koreans actually reach for.

As you’ve likely noticed, K-beauty has steadily grown from a niche category to the global mainstream over the last few years, thanks in large part to the power of social media. “While Amazon and TikTok are leading the K-beauty sales, the category is sure to see major growth this year as American consumers discover new products via social media, Korean culture (think: K-Pop and K-Drama), and in-store launches,” Sarah Chung Park, founder and CEO of Landing International, tells Vogue.

highlights.title: Tesla workers balk at training Optimus humanoid robots as replacements
highlights.summary: Tesla’s pivot from making electric cars to humanoid robots is facing challenges because of complex robot hands and disgruntled employees pushing back against training their robotic replacements.
body: As someone who frequently makes claims that fail to materialize, Musk has described the Optimus humanoid robot as potentially “the biggest product ever” during Tesla’s second-quarter 2026 earnings call. But he also acknowledged that making an autonomous humanoid robot capable of handling many different tasks is “one of the hardest things to solve”—and now extensive reporting by The Information has revealed multiple complications that Tesla is trying to tackle while developing general-purpose robots and scaling up for mass production.

Tesla’s Fremont factory in California has already stopped making the Model S sedan and Model X SUV as of May 2026, with the company switching both line workers and engineers over to working on Optimus, according to The Information.

highlights.title: Stormers win as Connacht falter on opening night
highlights.summary: Connacht fall to an opening-night defeat in the United Rugby Championship in Galway as the Stormers' power wore them down in the second half.
body: After a slow start to the opening 40 minutes, two quick-fire tries for the hosts turned the game on its head in the dying minutes of the first half.
However, a brilliant display of strength and game management from the Stormers meant that the points would be leaving with the South Africans after the first game of the new season.

The visitors started the game in fast fashion when Ruhan Nel almost touched down after six minutes, were it not for Ireland back Mack Hansen's last-ditch tackle to make sure the scores stayed level, before Jurie Matthee kicked between the posts to open the scoring for the evening.

Things would get worse for the Westerners when Warrick Gelant crossed for the first try of the game, when he chased a well-weighted kick after a period of pressure on the left wing for the Stormers, and Matthee slotted over the conversion.

highlights.title: Viral Resident Evil Stunt Footage Shows the Wild Way the 'Katamari Monster' Came to Life in Zach Cregger's Movie
highlights.summary: With Zach Cregger’s Resident Evil movie now in theaters, staff who worked on the film are sharing behind-the-scenes footage of how it all came together, including a jaw-dropping look at the stunt team behind one of its monsters. Warning: Spoilers for Resident Evil ahead!
body: Resident Evil is known for its wide variety of zombies, but some of the mutations we saw in Cregger’s version of events were brand-new and extremely gnarly. The main stalker monster of the film has been a hot topic of discussion within the games’ fanbase, with many affectionately dubbing it the ‘Katamari Monster.’

If you’ve seen the film and played the Katamari games, you’ll immediately understand why it’s been given this humorous moniker; its specific mutation includes some tentacle-like creatures that reach for other infected bodies and combine them into a mass of arms and legs that rolls around town, much like a Katamari.

Most viewers, myself included, figured this monster was a pure work of CGI. But astonishingly, this isn’t the case, as one of the stunt performers tasked with creating its movements proved in a now-viral Instagram post.

Jakub Hudlicky, a performer with Movement Production in the Czech Republic, published a series of videos showing himself and several other stuntpeople all strapped together with vests. Working together, the team made their way from one side of a soundstage to another, just like how the Katamari monster moved in Cregger’s film.

highlights.title: Thieves Stole ‘Nvidia’ Trailers. They Got 20 Tons of Sand
highlights.summary: They likely came for silicon—but left with silica.
body: On Thursday morning, a top executive at self-driving truck developer PlusAI received an unexpected congratulatory text message from an acquaintance. “I have been proud of you for your adventure and success at Plus. Just saw two of your trucks near my work place!:)” the message said.

But PlusAI’s trucks weren’t supposed to be near this person’s office, in Newark, California. As of the last the company knew, the trailers were docked outside its warehouse, half a mile away. Soon, according to a police statement, cops were on the scene to help recover the two trailers, emblazoned with logos for PlusAI and Nvidia, the most valuable company in the world. The two companies are working together on AI software and autonomous truck technology.

That’s when PlusAI employees gave police a hint as to why whoever hooked their own cabs up to the trailers and drove away might have abandoned the whole thing after breaking them open: Each trailer was full of about 20,000 pounds of sand.

“PlusAI uses simulated loads in its trailers to assist with research and development testing,” says Lauren Kwan, a company spokesperson. The trailers were recovered with “40,000 pounds of sand intact.”

highlights.title: Nations League: Kylian Mbappé injured after scoring France winner in Turkey
highlights.summary: France beat 10-man Turkey 1-0 to start Zidane era. Italy 0-2 Belgium, Georgia 0-1 Northern Ireland. Kylian Mbappé limped off with an apparent knee injury, moments after scoring France’s winner against Turkey in the Nations League on Friday.
body: The Real Madrid striker rifled in a low shot in the 55th minute after he was set up by Michael Olise. Soon after his record-extending 67th France goal, Mbappé sat on the ground and grimaced as he rubbed the area around his left knee.

The new France head coach, Zinedine Zidane, replaced Mbappé with Désiré Doué. In an encouraging sight, he was able to walk off the field of his own accord – but Zidane said afterwards that he expects his captain to return to Real Madrid for treatment.

“It’s not great. Unfortunately I think he [Mbappé] is going to have to go home. We don’t want to take any risks,” Zidane told French broadcaster TF1. “He overextended his knee while shooting. It’s not very encouraging.”

Jules Koundé hit the post for France before Turkey were reduced to 10 men, goalkeeper Ugurcan Cakir sent off for handling the ball outside his area after Bradley Barcola had been played through on goal.

highlights.summary: I'm currently blazing my way through my second Act One playthrough in Fire Emblem: Fortune's Weave, this time on Dietrich's route. It comes highly recommended by Polygon's own Josh Broadwell, and for good reason.
body: They are nasty, carnivorous seals with bulbous dangly noses, a far cry from the cuddly otters you see playing with beach balls and seashells. One of them even munches up Esmeralda's dad, but she's remarkably nonchalant about the whole thing. These things happen!

Elsewhere in the gaming world this week, Rockstar Games revealed a new box of Grand Theft Auto 6 collectibles that costs a whopping $400 and quite rudely does not include a copy of the game. That's because 1) Rockstar isn't releasing physical copies in the first place and 2) if people are willing to pay $400 for a pair of sunglasses, a ballcap, and some other low-value tat, I suppose you may as well let them.

Anyway, one of the items included in this box is a "Chunkee the Manatee Shot Glass," featuring a character from the in-universe animated show Macca the Gator, which has some serious BoJack Horseman vibes. Elsewhere in the promotional materials, you see various people wearing turquoise football jerseys emblazoned with Manatees branding, presumably Leonida's riff on the Miami Dolphins. Great Scott! It's sea beasts all the way down!

highlights.title: Boston Is One of America’s Best Sushi Cities—Here’s Where to Make a Reservation
highlights.summary: From lavish omakase counters with Hermès plates and a Michelin-star winner to unfussy, neighborhood gems, here are the Boston spots that our sushi snobs (yes, there are many here) rely on.
body: If there’s anything I know about Boston, it’s that this is a city that knows its seafood. Because of location and fishing heritage, we sling lobster rolls and oysters and fried clams by the bucket—so it should come as no surprise that sushi, too, has become a serious part of the city’s more upscale dining culture. Yes, travelers come here to experience our classic sea coast and clam shacks, but increasingly you’ll find that Boston has a robust enough sushi scene to excite international visitors, too—one that benefits not only from our abundant local fisheries, but also the international demand that make it possible to source special ingredients like fish flown in straight from Japan.
